find: The case was argued on January 6--7, 1964, and decided on March 9, 1964, together with \textit{Abernathy v.\ Sullivan}
replace: \textit{New York Times} was argued on January 6, 1964, and \textit{Abernathy v.\ Sullivan} on January 7, 1964. Both were decided on March 9, 1964
reason: The U.S. Reports assigns a separate argument date to each case.

find: the blogger's own creation of the controversy point the other way
replace: the fact that the bribery story itself cannot supply the notoriety needed to establish public-figure status point the other way
reason: The zoning controversy existed independently of the article. The defendant cannot turn the owner into a public figure by giving her notoriety through the allegedly defamatory publication.
Black's 'Malice, even as defined by the Court, is an elusive, abstract concept...' passage is on page 295.

find: Under \textit{Gertz}, the State may allow recovery
replace: Under \textit{Gertz}, as limited by \textit{Dun \& Bradstreet, Inc. v. Greenmoss Builders, Inc.}, 472 U.S.\ 749 (1985), the State may allow recovery
reason: Gertz barred presumed and punitive damages absent actual malice for all private-figure plaintiffs. The restriction of that rule to speech on matters of public concern comes from Dun & Bradstreet (plurality). The sentence blends the two decisions.
source: Gertz v. Robert Welch, Inc., 418 U.S. 323, 349 (1974); Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. v. Greenmoss Builders, Inc., 472 U.S. 749, 761 (1985) (CourtListener)
